d_07da39ff5f9f1183fee7.description: Net and gross exposure aggregated by primitive instrument identifier.

gross_value.description: Sum of absolute reporting-currency path values.

days.description:
Calendar days between `old_date` and `new_date`.

Always a calendar-day span, including under
[`TimeRollMode::BusinessDays`](crate::spec::TimeRollMode::BusinessDays):
the target date is business-day adjusted, but the span back to

d_0a9453006ca0409ae6dc.description:
Size and shape of one applied shock.

Sizes are the shock as requested on the (hierarchy-expanded) operation, in
that operation's own quote space, with the resolved location where the
engine produced one. Delivery adjustments that change how the request
reaches the market object — interpolation splits across neighbouring
knots, solve-to-par recalibration, first-order hazard shifts, clamping —
are reported in [`ApplicationReport::warnings`], not here.

oneOf.description:
One size applied to the whole target: a parallel curve or surface
shift, or the shock to a scalar price, an FX rate or a set of
instruments.

Triangular key-rate bump centred on one curve knot, emitted once per
resolved knot of a discount or inflation curve node shock.

time_years.description:
Knot time the bump is centred on, in years on the curve's own time
axis.

value.description:
Bump size delivered at that knot, in `unit`. For an off-knot tenor
matched by interpolation this is the knot's calibrated share of
the requested shock.

oneOf.description:
Node shocks delivered by rebuilding the curve in one step (forward,
par-CDS, commodity and volatility-index node shocks). Lists the nodes
as requested; the rebuilt curve is not echoed.

nodes.description: Requested `(tenor, size)` nodes in operation order.

expiries_years.description:
Surface grid expiries the shock was restricted to, in years, after
snapping the requested tenors to the grid. Absent when every
expiry is shocked.

strikes.description:
Strikes the shock was restricted to. Absent when every strike is
shocked.

oneOf.description: Base-correlation shock restricted to detachment points.

detachments_bp.description:
Detachment points the shock was restricted to, in basis points
(`300` = 3%), as supplied on the operation.

generic_epsilon.description:
Epsilon for generic floating-point comparisons (default: 1e-10).

Used for general numerical comparisons where higher tolerance is acceptable.

d_0f7858a8a073798bb651.description: Complete primitive decomposition with path, net, and gross views.

paths.description: Every primitive path before overlap netting.

d_11c88c8641cb7ae81898.description: Rich structured details attached to composite valuation results.

exposures.description: Recursive path-level and net/gross primitive exposures.

leg_results.description: Native and reporting-currency results for every top-level leg.

reporting_currency.description: Currency of all reported values and additive risk measures.

resolved_legs.description: Frozen top-level quantities used for this valuation.

state_effective_date.description: Effective date of the frozen holdings state used for pricing.

weighting_inputs.description: Scalar inputs retained when the state was resolved.

d_148bbe419288e7b68d26.description: Unit in which an applied shock's size is expressed.

oneOf.description:
Additive basis points of a rate or spread (`1.0` = 0.0001 in decimal
rate space).
Relative change in percent of the current level (`5.0` = +5%).

Additive change in the target's own quote units: volatility-index
points for a volatility-index curve, decimal correlation for base
correlation and structured-credit correlations (`0.02` = +0.02).

d_1a872a78f6334f77801f.description:
Finite-difference bump sizes in force for a metric request.

These are the values after layering the `valuations.sensitivities.v1`
configuration extension and the instrument's
`metric_pricing_overrides.bump_config` over the library defaults. Bumped
sensitivities are reported per unit bump (per 1bp, per 1 vol point), so
these sizes describe how the difference was taken, not the reporting unit.

A calculator with a fixed, documented shock of its own (for example an
analytic greek, or a metric whose rustdoc names its shock) does not read
these values.

adaptive_bumps.description:
Whether spot and volatility bumps are rescaled by volatility, time to
expiry and moneyness instead of applied at the fixed sizes above.

rate_bump_bp.description: Parallel interest-rate bump in basis points (1.0 = 1bp).

spot_bump_decimal.description: Spot bump as a decimal fraction of spot (0.01 = 1%).

vol_bump_decimal.description: Absolute volatility bump in decimal volatility (0.01 = 1 vol point).

ytm_bump_bp.description:
Yield bump in basis points for numerical yield duration and convexity.
Absent when each calculator keeps its own default shock.

d_20e530ddb3c6b466caf1.description:
Container for detailed execution traces of financial computations.

Traces are organized by type (calibration, pricing, waterfall) and contain
a sequence of domain-specific entries. Traces can be serialized to JSON for
inspection, debugging, or audit purposes.

Mutation is intentionally single-threaded through `&mut self`. If multiple
workers need to append to one trace, wrap it in external synchronization and
keep ordering semantics explicit at the call site.

truncated.description: Whether the trace was truncated due to size limits

d_23a59b5e3a559f1ea54d.description:
Finite JSON number that is strictly greater than zero.

This type is used by serde field adapters so runtime deserialization and
generated schemas enforce the same positive-number contract.

headroom.description: Cushion relative to threshold (positive => passing buffer)

meta.description: Audit stamp: numeric mode, rounding context, and FX policy in force.

d_2a8dbd04e24bb7848662.description: One requested curve-node shock, as written on the operation.

tenor.description: Tenor label of the node as supplied on the operation (for example `"5Y"`).

value.description:
Shock size requested at that tenor, in the enclosing
[`ShockMagnitude::Nodes`] unit.

d_329d437a8212bdfb6be2.description:
Identifies which family of curve an operation targets.

These variants map to the market data collections exposed by
`finstack_quant_core::market_data::context::MarketContext`.
They also determine which quoting and interpolation conventions apply when
downstream helpers extract rates or apply node shocks.

# Examples
```rust
use finstack_quant_scenarios::CurveKind;

let kind = CurveKind::Discount;
assert_eq!(format!("{:?}", kind), "Discount");
```

oneOf.description:
Commodity forward [`PriceCurve`](finstack_quant_core::market_data::term_structures::PriceCurve).

`bp` on parallel/node ops is percent of the price-curve forward
(`5.0` = +5%), not a rate basis-point shock. Looking up a
[`DiscountCurve`](finstack_quant_core::market_data::term_structures::DiscountCurve)
under this id is an error.

d_344a092481142c1669cc.description:
Complete portfolio valuation results.

Provides per-position valuations, totals by entity, and the grand total.

as_of.description: Valuation date carried through from the portfolio.

degraded_positions.description:
Positions whose valuation fell back to PV-only because requested risk
metrics could not be computed.

fx_collapse_policy.description:
FX policy applied when collapsing position values to the base currency.

Base-currency rollups use an explicit spot-equivalent conversion at
[`as_of`](Self::as_of) through the market FX matrix; this records the
applied [`FxConversionPolicy`] so the result envelope satisfies the
policy-visibility invariant (the FX strategy is stamped, not implied).

total_base_currency.description: Total portfolio value in base currency

d_35c446142142801cbb82.description:
Domain-specific trace entry types.

Each variant captures relevant details for different types of computations:
- Calibration: solver steps as generic computation steps
- Pricing: cashflow-level PV breakdowns
- Waterfall: step-by-step payment allocations

cashflow_amount.description: Cashflow amount (stored as f64 for JSON simplicity)

survival_probability.description:
Conditional survival probability to the payment date, `S(date) / S(as_of)`.

Present only for credit-risky valuations. `pv_amount` then also
includes the recovery leg, so it is not `cashflow_amount ×
discount_factor × survival_probability`.

d_3b714c6f9450267930ea.description: A volatility-surface dependency with the context needed for diagnostics.

reference_strike.description: Optional contractual strike used by local volatility diagnostics.

spot_id.description: Optional market-scalar id of the underlying spot paired with the surface.

d_482fa346c77e25f26a51.description: Stochastic pricing result for a structured credit deal.

clean_price.description:
Clean price (percent of the sum of current tranche balances),
UNADJUSTED for accrued interest.

This equals [`Self::dirty_price`]. The deal-level stochastic
result carries no per-tranche interest flows, so accrued cannot be
computed here (the same constraint documented on the accrued
calculator). It is reported unadjusted rather than fabricated: the
error is at most one period's accrued interest, in a known direction.
Use `tranche_metrics` when an accrued-adjusted clean price is
required.

dirty_price.description:
Dirty price (percent of the sum of current tranche balances),
including accrued interest.

This is the authoritative price: it is the present value of all future
cashflows from the valuation date, which by definition contains the
accrued portion of the next coupon. The face is the notes' current
balance, the same basis as the deterministic `dirty_price` metric,
so a deal whose notes total less than the pool prices near par rather
than at the note-to-pool ratio.

draw_option_cost.description:
Mean over paths of the draw option cost: the value to the deal of its
revolvers' simulated draws having been made at the contractual margin
instead of each path's fair spread, obtained per path as the present
value of the actual tranche cashflows less that of a counterfactual
run where every draw accrues at its fair spread. Negative when spreads
widen; zero for pools without stochastic revolvers.

draw_option_cost_paths.description:
Per-path draw option cost in path order (same currency as `npv`),
populated only for pools with stochastic revolvers.

expected_collateral_draws.description:
Mean over paths of the collateral draws funded through the reserve
account and principal collections (revolver utilization increases,
delayed draws and loan-equivalent draws at default).

npv.description: Net present value of the deal

num_paths.description:
Number of simulated scenario paths (`2 × pricing_mode.num_paths` with
antithetic pairing, `pricing_mode.num_paths` without).

pv_confidence_interval.description:
Two-sided 95% Student-t confidence interval for the mean PV, in the
NPV currency, using one fewer degree of freedom than the independent
estimator count. Coverage is approximate for non-Gaussian payoffs.

pv_std_error.description:
Sample standard error of the mean PV estimate, in the NPV currency.

Uses Bessel-corrected variance over independent estimators; each
antithetic pair contributes one mean observation.

unfunded_draw_path_fraction.description:
Fraction of paths on which a collateral draw could not be funded from
the reserve account and that period's principal collections (`0.0`
for pools without draws).

amount.description:
Monetary amount, carried on the wire as an exact decimal string rather
than a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit. Construction with
configuration applies the selected ingest scale; raw construction does not.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of `amount`. Arithmetic between two `Money` values
requires this to match; there is no implicit conversion.

d_4f9196221f8fbfd9bfe1.description:
Strongly-typed metric identifier.

Provides compile-time validation, autocomplete support, and safe refactoring
when metric names change. Covers bond, IRS, deposit, and risk metrics.

See unit tests and `examples/` for usage.

d_55fd8d302833a65d16f6.description:

mode.description: Explicitly selected rounding mode; absent when none was selected.

output_scale_by_currency.description: Validated output scale snapshot by currency code, with values in `0..=28`.

tolerances.description: Tolerance settings snapshot for floating-point comparisons.

d_67be71f4ec3ffee70c10.description:
A concrete market-data target changed while applying a scenario.

Targets are recorded from hierarchy-expanded operations together with the
effects that were actually accepted by the engine. Consequently, every
identifier is a resolved market identifier rather than an unresolved
hierarchy path or a best-effort reconstruction of the original spec.

oneOf.description: A discount, forward, credit, inflation, or commodity curve.

curve_id.description: Concrete identifier changed in that collection.

curve_kind.description: Curve family used to select the market-data collection.

oneOf.description: An equity or other scalar price entry.

base.description: Base currency strengthened or weakened by the operation.

quote.description: Quote currency used for the shocked rate.

d_6f90163da686371ca49e.description: Unified dependency container for instrument market data requirements.

credit_index_ids.description:
Credit-index aggregates resolved through `MarketContext::get_credit_index`.

These identifiers are distinct from direct hazard-curve IDs because a
credit index also carries base correlation and optional issuer curves.

fx_pairs.description: FX pairs required for pricing (spot matrices).

market_scalar_ids.description:
Scalar market-value identifiers resolved through `MarketContext::get_price`.

This includes tradable spots and non-price unitless scalars such as
continuous dividend yields. [`Self::series_ids`] is reserved for
`MarketContext::get_series` dependencies.

series_ids.description: Scalar time series identifiers (e.g., OHLC price series for realized variance).

volatility_dependencies.description: Typed volatility dependencies in deterministic insertion order.

generic_epsilon.description:
Epsilon for generic floating-point comparisons (default: 1e-10).

Used for general numerical comparisons where higher tolerance is acceptable.

d_85fe99734ff4d8a1aea4.description:
Authoritative change manifest produced while applying a scenario.

Readers use the manifest to invalidate only the market factors and
instruments that actually changed, while `all_dirty` provides a
conservative escape hatch for changes that cannot be represented precisely.

all_dirty.description:
Whether callers must conservatively treat every dependency as dirty.

This is set for effective time rolls because date-sensitive values can
change even when no explicit market or instrument target was mutated.

as_of_changed.description: Whether the execution context's effective valuation date changed.

changed_instrument_indices.description: Zero-based indices of portfolio instruments mutated in place.

market_targets.description: Concrete market-data targets changed by applied effects.

portfolio_shape_changed.description:
Whether instruments were inserted, removed, or reordered.

Scenario operations do not change portfolio shape, so this stays `false`.

d_979a918a504fe5c6f8f7.description:
Model-specific typed valuation details.

These details are for rich structured outputs that do not fit the scalar
`measures` map while still belonging in the standard valuation envelope.

oneOf.description: Recursive leg valuation and primitive exposure detail for a composite.
Scenario-waterfall structured credit stochastic pricing result.

FX-bearing instrument pricing metadata (forwards, options, quanto, …).

Surfaces the [`FxMatrix`](finstack_quant_core::money::fx::FxMatrix) lookup
chain that backed the spot rate used at pricing time, satisfying the
project-wide FX-policy-visibility invariant for instruments that
resolve their spot through the matrix.
Monte Carlo estimator and reproducibility metadata.

d_9ac3b1be80f4eff446fb.description:
How a valuation result was produced.

Stamped by [`crate::pricer::PricerRegistry::price_with_metrics`] on every
result so the number can be reproduced from the result plus the archived
market: the model that priced it, the date the caller asked for, the market
data the instrument declares, any scenario adjustment applied to the value,
and the bump sizes behind its sensitivities.

market_dependencies.description:
Curves, surfaces, scalars, FX pairs and series the instrument declares
it reads. Identifiers refer to the `MarketContext` the result was
priced against.

requested_as_of.description:
Valuation date the caller requested.

The result's `as_of` is the effective date after the instrument resolved
it (for example to the market's spot date); the two differ only when
the instrument moved it.

scenario_price_shock_decimal.description:
Scenario price shock already applied to `value`, as a decimal
(`-0.10` = the model value was multiplied by 0.90). Absent when the
value is the unadjusted model value.

sensitivity_bumps.description:
Bump sizes in force for the requested metrics. Absent when no metric
was requested.

d_9ca21aa74507178203bd.description:
Provider-selection purpose of a point-date FX query (record
CORE-CONVENTIONS-013 #1/#2).

The policy tells a provider which source purpose the rate serves; it does
not calculate dates or choose spot versus forward. There is no default:
every query names its policy. Period averages are not point queries; an
owner that needs one computes the oriented aggregate itself.

oneOf.description: The rate applicable on a cashflow's own date.
The rate applicable on a reporting period's closing date.

d_9dbe9a40fccc63c10676.description: One top-level leg result retained in composite valuation details.

instrument_id.description: Identifier of the top-level leg specification.

native_value.description: Quantity-scaled value in the underlying instrument's native currency.

quantity.description: Signed frozen leg quantity applied to the unit valuation.

reporting_value.description: Quantity-scaled value converted to the composite reporting currency.

valuation.description: Complete unit-instrument valuation, including nested details where applicable.

d_9de9bcf26fa2ccd01b1f.description: Numeric schema revision for contracts whose sole supported revision is v1.

d_a6f21a39d7967d35897d.description:
Finite JSON number that is strictly greater than zero.

This type is used by serde field adapters so runtime deserialization and
generated schemas enforce the same positive-number contract.

d_a7e13ac4f8bfd7d4f040.description:
Exact decimal encoded only as a JSON string.

Restoration routes through [`crate::decimal::parse_decimal`], the single
exact text-admission rule: JSON numbers, malformed text and inexact values
are rejected rather than rounded. Serialization writes canonical
fixed-point text with trailing zeros removed and signed zero normalized
(`"1.5"`, `"0"`), never scientific notation.

d_a923fe11dbdde3e69fd8.description: Level of a scalar market value immediately before and after a shock.

after.description: Stored level after the shock, in the same units.

before.description:
Stored level before the shock, in the scalar's own units (the amount
for a monetary price).

d_adb505b22deadbdfe62e.description: Reproducibility and convergence diagnostics for a Monte Carlo valuation.

brownian_bridge.description: Whether Brownian-bridge ordering was enabled for Sobol paths.

estimator_paths.description: Number of independent path estimators contributing to the mean.

make_whole_training_paths.description:
Independent paths used to fit state-conditional make-whole reference
values. Zero when no stochastic make-whole stage is required.

make_whole_training_simulated_paths.description:
Total factor paths simulated for state-conditional make-whole training,
including antithetic partners. Zero when that stage is absent.

model_key.description: Registered model used for the simulation.

seed.description: Deterministic random seed used for the run.

simulated_paths.description: Total number of simulated paths, including antithetic partners.

sobol.description: Whether Sobol quasi-random sampling was enabled.

standard_error.description:
Sampling standard error of the discounted PV mean in the result
currency. For LSMC valuations, this measures pricing-path uncertainty
under the frozen fitted exercise policy. It excludes regression
approximation, time-grid discretization, and model error.

time_grid.description: Simulation times in year fractions, including zero and maturity.

training_paths.description:
Number of independent paths used to fit an exercise or control policy.

Zero for Monte Carlo engines that do not have a separate training
stage.

training_simulated_paths.description:
Total factor paths simulated in the policy-training stage, including
antithetic partners. Zero when no policy is trained.

d_afddc625e94070f6fe94.description:
Strongly-typed instrument classification for pricer dispatch.

Each variant represents a distinct instrument type with its own pricing
logic and risk characteristics. Used by the pricing registry to route
instruments to appropriate pricer implementations.

oneOf.description: Fixed or floating-rate bond (plain vanilla, callable, amortizing).
CDS Index (portfolio credit protection, e.g., CDX, iTraxx).
CDS Tranche (mezzanine credit exposure via synthetic CDO).
Interest rate cap or floor (portfolio of caplets/floorlets).
Option on interest rate swap (European exercise).
Convertible bond (bond with embedded equity option).
Vanilla equity option (call or put on single stock or index).
FX variance swap (volatility exposure on FX).
Equity spot position (shares in single stock or fund).
Forward Rate Agreement (forward-starting interest rate contract).
Structured credit (ABS, RMBS, CMBS, CLO with tranches and waterfall).
Private markets fund (PE/credit fund with waterfall).
Asian option (payoff based on average price).
Barrier option (knock-in or knock-out on barrier cross).
Lookback option (payoff based on path extremum).
Quanto option (cross-currency option with quanto adjustment).
Cliquet option (ratchet option with periodic resets).
Range accrual note (coupon accrues when rate in range).
FX barrier option (FX option with knock-in/out barrier).
Term loan (optionally Delayed Draw Term Loan)
Real estate asset valuation (DCF or direct cap).
Levered real estate equity (asset minus financing).
Fixed Income Index Total Return Swap.
Bond future (futures on a deliverable bond basket with CTD mechanics).
Commodity option (option on commodity forward or spot).
Commodity Asian option (option on arithmetic/geometric average of commodity prices).
Commodity swaption (option on a fixed-for-floating commodity swap).
Commodity spread option (option on the spread between two commodities).
FX forward (outright forward, single exchange at maturity).
Agency MBS passthrough (FNMA, FHLMC, GNMA pools).
FX touch option (one-touch / no-touch American binary).
Target Redemption Note (path-dependent coupon with knockout).
CMS Spread Option (option on spread between two CMS rates).
Callable Range Accrual (range accrual with Bermudan call).
Generic resolved basket of signed underlying instrument quantities.
Linear listed future on a single or average observed price.
Exchange-listed future on a deliverable currency pair.
Exchange-listed equity or equity-index future, including fixed-currency quantos.
Listed equity total-return future quoted as an annualized financing spread.
Listed or bilateral option on an interest-rate futures price.
Exchange-listed option on an equity or equity-index futures contract.
Exchange-listed option on an FX futures contract.
Exchange-listed option on a commodity futures contract.
Exchange-listed option on a volatility-index futures contract.
Asset-backed facility (warehouse line against a collateral pool).

d_b2b64fea7715cf5d4700.description: FX pair identifier using base/quote currency ordering.

d_b38440a627738e14b971.description: Immutable resolved quantity for one top-level composite leg.

instrument_id.description: Identifier of the corresponding leg specification.

quantity.description: Signed quantity held from the state's effective date until the next rebalance.

d_b3a70f30000c75370aed.description:
A single warning emitted by an adapter, the engine, or a downstream helper.

New variants will be added over time; pattern matches on `Warning` should
always include a wildcard arm.

oneOf.description: Par-spread shocks used the approximation delta hazard = delta spread / (1 - recovery).

curve_id.description: Hazard curve affected by the approximate spread shock.

recovery_rate.description: Decimal recovery fraction used in the loss-given-default conversion.

oneOf.description:
A discount curve was resolved heuristically (currency-prefix or single-
curve fallback) instead of via an explicit `discount_curve_id`.

chosen_discount.description: The discount curve selected by the heuristic.

for_curve.description: Curve identifier the heuristic was applied to.

reason.description: Reason text describing the heuristic path.

oneOf.description:
A commodity price-curve shock was outside the typical percent-of-forward
stress range (approximately `[-80, +200]` percent).

detail.description:
Detail describing whether the trigger was a parallel or node shock
and which knot(s) were extreme.

oneOf.description: Equity identifier was missing from the market context; no bump applied.

Rate binding produced no statement update because the target node has
no explicit forecast values.

curve_id.description: Curve identifier from which the rate would have been extracted.

oneOf.description: Statement node had no forecast values to modify.
Model evaluator emitted a warning during re-evaluation.

detail.description: Free-text detail from the evaluator (already includes context).

oneOf.description:
FX shock left a non-pivot direct quote inconsistent with the pivot-
triangulated cross.

detail.description: Free-text detail naming the inconsistent pair and computed values.

oneOf.description:
Instrument shock fell back to attribute metadata because no pricing
override was exposed by the instrument's pricer.

inst_type.description: Canonical instrument type that could not apply the shock directly.

shock_kind.description: Whether the shock is a price (`"price"`) or spread (`"spread"`).

oneOf.description: Instrument shock found no instruments matching the filter.

filter_desc.description: Free-text description of the filter (e.g. `IndexMap` debug form).

oneOf.description:
Correlation shock found no `StructuredCredit` instruments with a
correlation structure.
Correlation bump clamped one or more correlation parameters.

detail.description: Detail string describing what was clamped.

oneOf.description:
A shock targeting a curve node by tenor had to extrapolate beyond the
curve's pillar range.

detail.description: Free-text describing the tenor and the gap.

oneOf.description:
An interpolated node bump split its shock across two pillars of a
par-CDS curve that is rebuilt by solve-to-par recalibration. On that
path the 1/Σw² delivery correction is only first-order — the weighted
targets are snapped to the nearest calibration quotes before
re-solving, so the realized shock at the requested tenor may differ
from the requested size. Direct-shift curves (discount, inflation,
forward, commodity) calibrate onto the native interpolant and do not
emit this warning. Use `TenorMatchMode::Exact` at pillar tenors for
pillar-accurate par-CDS bucket risk.

detail.description: Free-text describing the tenor and adjacent pillars.

oneOf.description: Bucket-correlation shock matched no detachment buckets.
Vol-surface negative bucket shock that may produce non-positive vols.

bucket.description: Whether this was a parallel (`false`) or bucket (`true`) shock.

oneOf.description:
A hierarchy-targeted operation expanded to zero curves. This is almost
always a configuration mistake — the target path exists but has no
curves attached to it, or the tag filter excluded everything.

target_path.description: Hierarchy path the operation targeted, joined with `/`.

oneOf.description:
A hierarchy-resolved identifier was skipped because it does not exist
in the market collection targeted by the operation kind (e.g. a
`HierarchyCurveParallelBp { curve_kind: Discount }` matched an id that
is an equity price or vol surface, not a discount curve). The remaining
resolved identifiers are still applied.

curve_id.description: The resolved identifier that was skipped.

oneOf.description:
An instrument's valuation failed while computing carry during a
`TimeRollForward` operation. The instrument is excluded from the
roll-forward carry aggregation but the roll itself proceeds.

integration_method.description: CDS integration method actually used, when applicable.

model_key.description: Registered model key used by the pricer.

fx_policy_applied.description: Optional FX policy applied by the computing layer (human-readable key).

numeric_mode.description:
Numeric engine mode used to produce the results.

Always [`NUMERIC_MODE_F64`] today; a plain string so result
envelopes stay wire-compatible across host languages.

parallel.description:
Whether the producing computation ran in parallel.

Serial results omit the field entirely so existing payloads and golden
files stay byte-identical.

rounding.description: Rounding context snapshot applied to IO boundaries.

timestamp.description:
Timestamp when result was computed (ISO 8601 format).
Useful for audit trails and reproducibility.

version.description: Finstack Quant library version used to produce the result.

d_bdf84b73c34f6ec51af5.description:
Exact decimal encoded only as a JSON string.

Restoration routes through [`crate::decimal::parse_decimal`], the single
exact text-admission rule: JSON numbers, malformed text and inexact values
are rejected rather than rounded. Serialization writes canonical
fixed-point text with trailing zeros removed and signed zero normalized
(`"1.5"`, `"0"`), never scientific notation.

fx_policy_applied.description: Optional FX policy applied by the computing layer (human-readable key).

numeric_mode.description:
Numeric engine mode used to produce the results.

Always [`NUMERIC_MODE_F64`] today; a plain string so result
envelopes stay wire-compatible across host languages.

parallel.description:
Whether the producing computation ran in parallel.

Serial results omit the field entirely so existing payloads and golden
files stay byte-identical.

rounding.description: Rounding context snapshot applied to IO boundaries.

timestamp.description:
Timestamp when result was computed (ISO 8601 format).
Useful for audit trails and reproducibility.

version.description: Finstack Quant library version used to produce the result.

d_c0886912a762c44d0759.description:
One shock the engine applied, in application order.

[`ScenarioChangeManifest`] says *which* targets changed (deduplicated, for
cache invalidation); this says *by how much*. A target shocked by several
effects has one entry per effect.

applies_to.description: Market target or instruments the shock was applied to.

level_change.description:
Stored level before and after the shock.

Present only for scalar price targets
([`ScenarioMarketTarget::EquityPrice`]), where both levels are read
from the market context around the mutation. Absent for FX, curves,
surfaces and instruments.

shock.description: Size, unit and shape of the shock.

amount.description:
Monetary amount, carried on the wire as an exact decimal string rather
than a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit. Construction with
configuration applies the selected ingest scale; raw construction does not.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of `amount`. Arithmetic between two `Money` values
requires this to match; there is no implicit conversion.

d_ccd53ca701e8c5bb4008.description:
Metadata for FX-bearing valuation paths (FX forwards, FX options, quanto).

Captures the FX policy applied at pricing time so downstream audit /
reconciliation can trace whether a quoted rate came from a direct
market quote or via triangulation through the matrix pivot currency.
Mirrors the "FX policy visibility" invariant in `ARCHITECTURE.md`: the
applied conversion strategy is recorded per layer (valuations, statements,
portfolio).

fx_triangulated.description:
`true` when the FX spot was obtained via triangulation through the
[`FxMatrix`](finstack_quant_core::money::fx::FxMatrix) pivot currency
rather than a direct quote. Mirrors
[`FxRateResult.triangulated`](finstack_quant_core::money::fx::FxRateResult).
`None` when the instrument resolved spot from an explicit market
scalar (`fx_spot_id`) rather than the matrix.

d_d361ff539fd6936d76af.description: ISO 8601 calendar date encoded as a `YYYY-MM-DD` JSON string.

d_d5837ae057e724b8713e.description:
Pricing model selection for the pricer registry.

Determines which mathematical model is used to price an instrument.
Each model has different computational characteristics and accuracy
profiles for different instrument types.

# Model Categories

## Analytical Models
- [`Discounting`](Self::Discounting): Simple present value discounting
- [`Black76`](Self::Black76): Black-76 formula for options
- [`Normal`](Self::Normal): Bachelier (normal) model for rate options

## Tree Models
- [`Tree`](Self::Tree): Binomial/trinomial lattice
- [`HullWhite1F`](Self::HullWhite1F): Hull-White one-factor short rate

## Credit Models
- [`HazardRate`](Self::HazardRate): Fractional-recovery hazard-rate pricing
- [`RatesCredit`](Self::RatesCredit): Joint short-rate and hazard-rate pricing

## Monte Carlo Models
- [`MonteCarloGBM`](Self::MonteCarloGBM): GBM simulation
- [`MonteCarloHeston`](Self::MonteCarloHeston): Heston stochastic vol
- [`MonteCarloThreeFactor`](Self::MonteCarloThreeFactor): revolver
  utilization, short-rate and credit-spread simulation

## Exotic Analytical
- [`BarrierBSContinuous`](Self::BarrierBSContinuous): Reiner-Rubinstein barriers
- [`AsianGeometricBS`](Self::AsianGeometricBS): Geometric Asian (exact)
- [`AsianTurnbullWakeman`](Self::AsianTurnbullWakeman): Arithmetic Asian (approx)

# Examples

```rust
use finstack_quant_valuations_core::pricer::ModelKey;

// Select appropriate model for instrument type
let model = ModelKey::Discounting;  // For bonds
let model = ModelKey::Black76;      // For caps/floors
let model = ModelKey::MonteCarloGBM; // For path-dependent exotics

// Parse from string
let model: ModelKey = "black76".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(model, ModelKey::Black76);
```

oneOf.description:
Present value discounting of projected cashflows.

Used for: bonds, swaps, deposits, repos, forwards.

Binomial or trinomial tree for callable/putable instruments.

Used for: callable bonds, Bermudan options.

Black-76 lognormal model for forward-based options.

Used for: caps, floors, swaptions, FX options, commodity options.

Hull-White one-factor short rate model.

Used for: callable bonds with OAS, Bermudan swaptions.

Hazard rate model for credit instruments.

Used for: CDS, CDS indices, and non-callable credit-risky bonds.

Joint short-rate and hazard-rate model for credit-risky bonds.

Used for: callable, puttable, return-floor, and straight bonds whose
rates and credit dynamics must be valued on one calibrated path.

Bachelier (normal) model for rate options.

Used for: inflation caps/floors, options on rates near zero.

Monte Carlo with Geometric Brownian Motion.

Used for: path-dependent options, exotics requiring simulation.

Monte Carlo with Heston stochastic volatility.

Used for: options requiring volatility smile dynamics.

Monte Carlo with Hull-White 1F rates.

Used for: Bermudan swaptions, CMS options.

Monte Carlo with joint utilization, short-rate and credit-spread
factors.

Used for: revolving credit facilities with a stochastic draw/repay
specification (mean-reverting utilization, a deterministic or
Hull-White short rate, and a market-anchored or CIR credit spread).

Reiner-Rubinstein continuous barrier formulas.

Used for: equity/FX barrier options with continuous monitoring.

Kemna-Vorst exact geometric Asian formula.

Used for: geometric average Asian options.

Turnbull-Wakeman approximation for arithmetic Asians.

Used for: arithmetic average Asian options.

Conze-Viswanathan lookback option formulas.

Used for: lookback options with continuous monitoring.

Quanto BS with drift adjustment.

Used for: quanto options (cross-currency).

FX barrier with Reiner-Rubinstein mapping.

Used for: FX barrier options.

Heston semi-analytical via Fourier transform.

Used for: European options requiring stochastic vol.

Merton structural credit Monte Carlo with PIK support.

Used for: PIK bonds, credit-risky bonds with structural default model.

Monte Carlo with Schwartz-Smith two-factor commodity model.

Used for: commodity options requiring mean-reverting short-term dynamics.

Static replication via a portfolio of vanilla options.

Used for: CMS options (replicates the payoff with a smile-consistent
swaption portfolio, capturing all convexity orders beyond Hagan's
first-order approximation).

LMM/BGM Monte Carlo with predictor-corrector discretization.

Used for: Bermudan swaptions, exotic rate derivatives requiring
multi-factor forward rate dynamics.

Structured-credit stochastic scenario waterfall model.

Used for: ABS/CLO/RMBS/CMBS tranche PVs with path-level waterfall cashflows.

Bond future clean-price proxy model.

Used for: bond futures when only the current CTD clean-price proxy is
available. This is intentionally separate from [`Discounting`](Self::Discounting)
because it does not model delivery carry, invoice economics, or delivery
optionality.

Monte Carlo with rough Bergomi (rBergomi) stochastic volatility.

Used for: European/exotic equity options requiring rough volatility
dynamics with fractional Brownian motion.

Monte Carlo with rough Heston stochastic volatility.

Used for: European/exotic equity options requiring rough Heston
dynamics with Volterra-driven variance.

Rough Heston semi-analytical via fractional Riccati Fourier transform.

Used for: European equity options with rough Heston dynamics,
using Lewis (2000) single-integral Fourier inversion.

1D Crank-Nicolson finite difference PDE solver.

Used for: European/American equity options, barrier options,
FX options. Names the scheme family: production pricers run
Rannacher-damped CN (implicit start-up steps, Rannacher 1984),
with a penalty method for early exercise.

2D ADI (Craig-Sneyd) finite difference PDE solver.

Used for: Heston stochastic volatility, local-stochastic vol,
and other 2D pricing problems. Splits the 2D PDE into
directional tridiagonal sweeps with explicit cross-derivative.

Bloomberg CDSO numerical-quadrature model for credit-default-swap
options.

Reference: Bloomberg L.P. Quantitative Analytics, *Pricing Credit
Index Options*, March 2012 (DOCS 2055833 ⟨GO⟩). The model
preserves the lognormal-spread assumption of the original
Black-on-spreads model but solves `O = P(t_e) · E[(V_te + H(K) +
D)+]` by numerical integration over the lognormal density. The
lognormal mean `m` is calibrated by Brent root finding so that
`F_0 = E[V_te]` (the no-knockout clean forward value); `H(K)` is
the strike-adjustment term `ξN(c − K)A(K)`; `D` is the realized
loss settlement. The closed-form Black-on-spreads model was
decommissioned on the Bloomberg CDSO terminal in 2010.

Used for: CDS options (`InstrumentType::CdsOption`).
Nearest; an exact midpoint goes to the even coefficient.

Nearest; an exact midpoint increases absolute magnitude. Other
fractions round to nearest (`1.1` -> `1`), not away from zero.

attach_pct.description: Attachment point in percent of the capital structure (0 = first loss).

credit_duration.description: Credit duration (price sensitivity to credit spread)

detach_pct.description: Detachment point in percent of the capital structure (100 = most senior).

draw_option_cost.description:
This tranche's share of the deal's draw option cost: the mean over
paths of its present value on the actual run less that on the
counterfactual run where revolver draws accrue at their fair spread.
Tranche shares sum to the deal's `draw_option_cost` on every path.

paths_with_principal.description:
Number of simulated paths on which the tranche received any
principal (the paths `wal` averages over).

price_pct.description:
Mean present value as a percent of the tranche's current balance at
the valuation date (100 = par); `0.0` for a fully retired tranche.

wal.description:
Weighted-average life (WAL, years) averaged over the paths on which
the tranche received principal; `0.0` when it never did.

oneOf.description: Nearest; an exact midpoint goes to the even coefficient.

Nearest; an exact midpoint increases absolute magnitude. Other
fractions round to nearest (`1.1` -> `1`), not away from zero.

applied_shocks.description:
Size of every market and instrument shock applied, in application
order: one entry per accepted effect, so the entries reconcile with
[`changes`](Self::changes) (every market target named there appears
here at least once, and the instrument indices here union to
`changes.changed_instrument_indices`).

Statement-forecast operations, rate bindings and the time roll are not
listed. Empty when the scenario applied no market or instrument shock,
and on reports deserialized from JSON written before this field
existed.

changes.description: Authoritative metadata describing the state changed by applied effects.

expanded_operations.description:
Number of direct (non-hierarchy) operations produced after hierarchy
expansion and resolution-mode deduplication. No-match expansion and
deduplication can make this smaller than `user_operations`. Because
`operations_applied` counts effects rather than operations, the two
counters are not directly comparable.

meta.description:
Audit stamp describing the numeric mode, rounding context, and FX
policy under which the scenario was applied.

operations_applied.description:
Number of effects successfully applied to the execution context.

One user-level operation can produce zero, one, or many effects after
hierarchy expansion and target resolution. This low-level effect count
is therefore not an operation-coverage ratio; inspect `changes` and
`warnings` to determine which targets changed or were skipped.

time_roll.description:
Roll-forward report from the Phase 0 `TimeRollForward` operation,
when the scenario contained one. Carries the per-instrument carry
decomposition and the new valuation date; instruments whose valuation
failed during the roll are also surfaced as
[`Warning::TimeRollInstrumentFailed`] entries in `warnings`.

user_operations.description:
Number of user-provided `OperationSpec` entries in the scenario
(before hierarchy expansion and deduplication).

d_e33f6bff4d9598cfee56.description:
Result of valuing a single position.

Holds both native-currency and base-currency valuations along with
the underlying [`ValuationResult`].

fx_rate.description:
Spot FX rate applied to collapse [`value_native`](Self::value_native)
into [`value_base`](Self::value_base): units of the portfolio base
currency per one unit of the native currency, observed at the
valuation date, so `value_native × fx_rate = value_base` (up to the
base currency's `Money` rounding).

Absent when the native currency is the base currency (no FX lookup is
made).

fx_triangulated.description:
Whether [`fx_rate`](Self::fx_rate) was built by triangulating through
the FX matrix's pivot currency (`true`) or read from a direct or
inverse quote (`false`).

Absent exactly when `fx_rate` is absent.

inapplicable_metrics.description:
Metrics on the portfolio menu that this position's instrument type has
no calculator for, and which were therefore never requested of it.

A portfolio metric list is a menu offered to a heterogeneous book (see
[`RequestedMetrics`]), so this records the per-position narrowing that
makes such a list usable. It is not a failure report: unlike
[`PortfolioValuation::degraded_positions`] and
[`PortfolioMetrics::skipped_metrics`](crate::metrics::PortfolioMetrics::skipped_metrics),
nothing here could have been computed and was not. An entry means the
model gives this instrument type no such exposure, so the position
contributes nothing to that metric's portfolio total by construction.

Listed in menu order. Empty for a position that supports the whole menu.

metric_scale.description:
Linear scaling factor to apply to summable risk measures.

This mirrors the economic position size and sign used for PV scaling,
but is kept separate so non-summable metrics such as YTM remain
unscaled at the position drill-down level.

risk_error.description: Original metrics failure message when the valuation fell back to PV-only.

risk_metrics_complete.description:
Whether every risk metric requested *of this position* was computed
successfully.

The requested set is the portfolio metric menu narrowed to what this
position's instrument type supports, so structural narrowing does not
clear this flag; the narrowed-away entries are listed on
[`inapplicable_metrics`](Self::inapplicable_metrics). `false` means a
supported metric failed to compute and the position fell back to
PV-only.

valuation_result.description: Full valuation result with metrics (including computed risk measures).

value_base.description: Value converted to portfolio base currency

value_native.description: Value in the instrument's native currency

d_e567683d30a4c26c8269.description: Collection of curves used by an instrument, categorized by market role.

credit_curves.description: Credit/hazard curves used by the instrument.

discount_curves.description: Discount curves used by the instrument (including primary and foreign).

forward_curves.description: Forward/projection curves used by the instrument.

inflation_curves.description: Inflation curves or published inflation indices used by the instrument.

d_ea44f9fc62fb5d9eee49.description: Path-level primitive exposure in a resolved composite tree.

measures.description: Reporting-currency additive risk measures for this path.

path.description: Composite and leg identifiers from the root to the primitive.

quantity.description: Signed primitive quantity after multiplying every nested state quantity.

value.description: Reporting-currency signed value for this path.

d_efef57815a2be6cc006b.description: Canonical valuation result containing PV and typed metrics.

covenants.description:
Covenant compliance results for structured products.

Present only for instruments with covenants (loans, structured credit).
Each covenant is keyed by its identifier with pass/fail status and details.

explanation.description:
Optional computation explanation trace.

Requested with `PricingOptions::with_explain`. For discounting and
hazard-rate valuations it holds one `cashflow_pv` entry per projected
cashflow, reconciled to `value`; for other models it holds a single
`computation_step` entry saying no per-flow decomposition exists.

instrument_id.description: Unique identifier for the priced instrument.

measures.description:
Computed risk measures and financial metrics.

Contains **derived risk metrics** such as DV01, Delta, Vega, etc.
The present value (PV) is **not** included here - it is available
in the `value` field above.

Keys are strongly-typed metric IDs (serialized as strings such as
"ytm", "dv01", "delta"). Use `MetricId` helpers for consistent lookups.

# Interpretation

Entries in this map are heterogeneous by design:
- some are currency amounts (`jump_to_default`)
- some are currency-per-bump sensitivities (`dv01`, `vega`, `rho`)
- some are decimal rates or probabilities (`ytm`, `default_probability`)
- some are ratios or counts (`tvpi_lp`, `constituent_count`)

Always interpret a measure together with its [`MetricId`] contract.

meta.description:
Calculation metadata and policy stamps.

Contains:
- Numeric mode (Decimal vs f64)
- Rounding context and precision
- FX policy for cross-currency calculations
- Calculation timing information

provenance.description:
How the result was produced: model, requested date, declared market
dependencies, scenario adjustment and sensitivity bump sizes.

Stamped by the pricer registry. Absent on results constructed directly.

schema_version.description: Required wire-format schema version. Only numeric `1` is accepted.

d_efef57815a2be6cc006b.title: Valuation Result

d_f1eec8c72cbed58783bc.description: What one applied shock was applied to.

oneOf.description:
A resolved market-data target; the same value the shock contributed to
[`ScenarioChangeManifest::market_targets`].

target.description: Concrete market-data target that was shocked.

oneOf.description: Instruments of the supplied inventory mutated in place.

indices.description:
Zero-based inventory indices of the instruments the shock changed,
ascending.

d_fcd765f028a63b1f206f.description:
Stochastic pricing mode.

Monte Carlo is the only engine: each scenario path draws its monthly
systematic factors from a seeded Philox substream and runs the full deal
waterfall. The mode is echoed on
[`StochasticPricingResult::pricing_mode`]
so a result records the estimator count it was produced with.

Test coverage:
`tests/instruments/structured_credit/unit/{stochastic_pricing_tests,stochastic_tranche_pv_tests}`
plus the convergence tests.

antithetic.description: Pair each estimator's path with its sign-flipped mirror.

num_paths.description:
Number of independent estimators; must be at least two to estimate
sampling uncertainty. With `antithetic` each estimator averages a
`(Z, -Z)` pair, so the engine prices `2 × num_paths` scenario paths.
Sample standard error and the Student-t interval use this estimator
count, with `num_paths - 1` degrees of freedom.
